frozen_original.title: Trump Calls Fauci 'Dr. Death' and Claims He Funded COVID Creation (2023)
frozen_original.synopsis: Following Dr. Anthony Fauci's retirement from the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases in December 2022, Donald Trump intensified attacks on the nation's most prominent infectious disease expert, calling him 'Dr. Death' and repeatedly claiming Fauci had funded the creation of COVID-19 through gain-of-function research at the Wuhan Institute of Virology. Trump called for Fauci to be prosecuted and jailed. While legitimate scientific debate exists about specific NIH funding grants to EcoHealth Alliance, the claim that Fauci personally funded COVID's creation as a bioweapon was unsupported by intelligence or scientific evidence. Congress investigated the NIH grants and found no evidence of deliberate pathogen creation. Trump's attacks on Fauci generated death threats against the scientist and his family, requiring permanent security protection.

frozen_original.title: Trump Withdraws from Paris Climate Agreement
frozen_original.synopsis: On June 1, 2017, Trump announced the United States would withdraw from the Paris Climate Agreement, the landmark 2015 global accord in which 195 nations committed to reducing greenhouse gas emissions to limit global warming. Trump falsely claimed the agreement disadvantaged American workers and economy, even though it was non-binding. The withdrawal was condemned by world leaders, corporate CEOs, governors, and mayors across the political spectrum. European leaders declared they would not renegotiate. Scientists warned the U.S. withdrawal would accelerate global temperature rise and undermine the diplomatic framework for climate action. The U.S. became one of only three countries outside the agreement. The decision was widely described as an abdication of global leadership and an act of willful environmental destruction.

frozen_original.title: FBI under Patel begins monitoring mosques and Muslim community organizations
frozen_original.synopsis: Under Kash Patel's leadership, the FBI reinstituted surveillance programs targeting mosques and Muslim community organizations, reviving religious profiling and First Amendment violations. The program assigned FBI agents to regularly monitor sermons, track attendees, and develop informants inside Muslim communities across the United States. The move echoed post-9/11 surveillance abuses and was condemned by Muslim civil rights organizations as a return to discriminatory religious profiling that had previously been found to produce no actionable intelligence.
